title: Mr Tom Gutteridge — General Osteopathic Council decision (2025-11-04)
text:
Case No: 963/7951

BEFORE THE INVESTIGATING COMMITTEE OF
THE GENERAL OSTEOPATHIC COUNCIL

IN THE MATTER OF:

GENERAL OSTEOPATHIC COUNCIL (GOsC)

and

TOM GUTTERIDGE (Registrant)

Registrant Undertakings to the IC
4 November 2025

1. I, Tom Gutteridge of my own volition to restrict my practice by making the
Undertakings set out below until the final determination of the allegations made
against me, to assure the Committee that I in the intervening period will not
pose a risk to patients, the public or reputation of the profession.

2. I undertake to work with a chaperone with every female patient. I will not use
any massage as a form of treatment. This means that I will not massage any
female patient which could be determined as prolonged touch with the use of
oils.

3. I undertake to strictly comply with the restrictions as particularised in these
Undertakings until the final determination of the allegations against me by a
Committee of the General Osteopathic Council (‘the GOsC’) or until such
other date as may be stipulated by the Committee.

4. I undertake to immediately notify the GOsC if I become aware that I may not be
able to comply with the restrictions in these Undertakings.

Case No: 963/7951

5. The above Undertakings will ensure that I am able to continue to practice in
a safe and effective manner and that the risk of repetition of the alleged conduct
and behaviour giving rise to these proceedings would be minimal.

6. I understand and accept that the Undertakings constitute a solemn promise to
the Committee as to conduct of my practice and behavior and that a failure
to comply with the Undertakings made may amount to Unacceptable
Professional Conduct.

7. I consent to the publication of the Undertakings on the GOsC website.

8. I consent to the provision of the Undertakings to any person that
the GOsC considers appropriate in the public interest.

Signed (Registrant): TOM GUTTERIDGE …………..

Date: …04/11/2025 ………………………..
